name: SLOVAKIA

flag.title: Slovak Tricolour
flag.note: White, blue, red with double-cross shield

lead: Slovakia is a small country with big mountains, mysterious caves and ancient castles. It has more castles per person than almost anywhere on Earth. Brown bears roam the Carpathian forests.

facts.label: Land area
facts.sub: About the size of Costa Rica

sections.wows: 7 things to make you go wow

geo: Slovakia sits in the Carpathian mountains. In the north, the High Tatras rise like shark teeth. The top peak, Gerlachovský štít, is 2,654 m.
Over 7,000 caves have been found under Slovakia, and six are UNESCO listed. The Demänovský system under the Low Tatras is 43 km long. It is the longest cave in the Carpathians.
animals: Around 1,000 brown bears roam the Carpathian forests, among the EU's highest densities. Eurasian lynx pad silently through old spruce woods.
The Tatra chamois, a nimble goat-antelope, lives on high rocky ridges. Its numbers fell below 200 around 2000. Protection brought them to over 1,400.
culture: Each village once had its own songs, costumes and wooden churches. Bryndzové halušky, potato dumplings with sheep's cheese and bacon, is the national dish.
Ice hockey is a national obsession. Slovakia won the world championship in 2002. Over 180 castles, ruined or restored, dot the hills.
history: Slavic tribes settled here in the 5th century. In 863, missionaries Cyril and Methodius brought the first Slavic alphabet to Great Moravia. Later, Slovakia spent about 1,000 years in the Kingdom of Hungary.
In 1918, Slovakia and the Czechs formed Czechoslovakia. The peaceful Velvet Revolution ended Communist rule in 1989. On 1 January 1993, Slovakia and Czechia parted as friendly nations.
wows: Slovakia has over 180 castles in an area smaller than Costa Rica.
Bratislava is the only capital that borders two other countries, Austria and Hungary.
The Demänovský cave system is 43 km long, the longest in the Carpathians.
Bryndza sheep's cheese has EU Protected status, like Champagne or Parmesan.
Bratislava's UFO Bridge has a flying-saucer restaurant 85 m above the Danube.
The Tatra chamois lives only in the Tatras and grew from under 200 to over 1,400.
Slovak inventor Štefan Banič patented the first practical parachute in 1914.

myths.fact: A bear's winter sleep is light. It can wake and wander out, and mothers give birth in the den.

myths.myth: Castles were cosy homes for kings
myths.fact: Most castles were built for defence. They were cold, damp and draughty, with small windows.
